shots.title: THE DAY THAT OUTLASTS THE YEAR
shots.purpose: Anchor the paradox on the planet itself before any numbers arrive
shots.claim: on Venus a single day lasts longer than the entire year
shots.evidence: hero plate of Venus in deep space + title card
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: stillness first so the paradox lands clean
shots.transition_reason: cut to space-scale as narration gives the two numbers

shots.purpose: Give both numbers at planetary scale before the diagram race
shots.claim: rotation 243 Earth days vs orbit 224.7 days
shots.motion_reason: lateral drift: slow progress matches the slow spin
shots.transition_reason: cut to diagram as narration says watch the race

shots.purpose: Build the race step by step: lap first, turn second, verdict last
shots.claim: the 224.7-day orbit completes before the 243-day rotation
shots.evidence: D1_race stages: orbit baseline, then sweep + lagging spin arrow, then verdict
shots.motion_reason: static hold; the staged diagram build is the motion
shots.transition_reason: cut to the same diagram family for the Earth contrast

shots.purpose: Contrast with Earth on one honest scale so the Venus bars need no words
shots.claim: Earth: 1-day spin vs 365-day orbit; Venus bars invert the ratio
shots.evidence: D2_compare stages: Earth baseline bars, then Venus bars with day longer than year
shots.motion_reason: static hold; bar growth carries the argument
shots.transition_reason: cut back to the planet for the backwards-spin detail

shots.purpose: Show the consequence, not just the fact: a sun rising from the wrong side
shots.claim: Venus rotates retrograde; the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east
shots.evidence: surface plate + circle highlight on the western horizon
shots.motion_reason: punch-in on the horizon as the sun is named
shots.transition_reason: cut to the dawn plate for the sunrise-to-sunrise count

shots.purpose: Give the practical day length people can feel
shots.claim: solar day on Venus is about 117 Earth days
shots.evidence: dawn plate + 117-days number pop under chapter chrome
shots.motion_reason: slow drift along the cloud tops — a day passing
shots.transition_reason: cut to the dawn-count diagram for the year conclusion

shots.purpose: Turn 117 days into the year-dawn conclusion
shots.evidence: D3_dawncount stages: sunrise-to-sunrise bar, then 1.92 dawns conclusion
shots.motion_reason: static hold; annotation builds over the plate
shots.transition_reason: cut to the collision plate for the open question

shots.purpose: Present the open question honestly: impact hypothesis, tidal drag, no consensus
shots.claim: cause of the slow retrograde spin is unsettled; leading hypotheses include an ancient impact and atmospheric tidal drag
shots.motion_reason: slow drift through debris arcs — unsettled history
shots.transition_reason: cut to the quiet payoff plate for the closing line

shots.end_card: ON VENUS, THE YEAR ALWAYS WINS
shots.purpose: Land the paradox as the ending: the year finishes before the day does
shots.claim: the year always wins the race
shots.evidence: dusk-crescent plate + end card, no call to action
shots.motion_reason: pull-back: the frame lets go of the viewer
